## 4. IS THE TOTAL STILL 53?

**Yes — but the sum is not evidence of coverage.**

60 classification entries − 3 explicitly non-failing = 57 failing-assertion entries. `bracket-body-corpus.test.js` contributes 9 entries across 5 tests (multi-assertion); every other file is one entry per test. 57 − 9 + 5 = **53**. Per-file: mt 8, extract 7, bracket-body 5, alt 5, legacy 4, mt-gating 4, sweep 4, bracket-delta 3, alt-corpus 2, equation-seam 2, module-sections 2, pipeline-integration 2, ctx-invariants 2, dom-comparison 1, m68710-table 1, robustness 1 = 53 across 16 files.

**Be blunt: this arithmetic can only detect double-counting, never a missed failure.** An unclassified failing test leaves the sum equal to whatever was classified. Only **three of sixteen** files have a per-file vitest count in the record (mt 8/49, alt 5/21, mt-gating 4/33) — all three match. The other **thirteen are unconfirmed**. The old extractor's lazy regex treated the self-closing tag as an OPENING tag and ran to the next `</emphasis>`, emitting `(a)[[i: 3d;]]`; body ' 3d;' equals no source <emphasis> text, so E2 correctly tripped. The re-extract emits `(a) 3[[i:d;]]` — body 'd;' equals the source emphasis text exactly. ▶ THE MARKERS WERE FIXED, NOT DROPPED: E2's own unit (comparable marker bodies, from its message) GREW 350 → 366 for this module. All 55 misaligned modules ALSO have at least one MISSING auto-N id, so inject refuses every one of them (silent-write set = 0, loud set = 55, clean set = 115). This is not a lucky null: a uniform shift of k means the top k EN auto-ids exceed max(IS auto-id), so a nonzero shift ALWAYS produces at least k orphans. The completeness gate is therefore a RELIABLE canary. Confirmed on disk: 34f870ac wrote only 12 chemistry 03-translated files and a22120c8 only 3; `books/efnafraedi-2e/03-translated/mt-preview/ch01/m68690.cnxml` is still from b1541400, an older internally-consistent vintage.

disputes.reasoning:
I confirmed every substantive claim in the finding, with stronger instruments than it used — and then found the one thing it got wrong: THE RENUMBERING IS NOT NECESSARY FOR THIS TEST TO FAIL, so the regression it discovered is not this test's finding.

CAUSATION. m68690's 13 recorded misses are 4 `alt:` + 9 `entry:auto-N`. The 4 alt misses are wholly independent of the auto-N misalignment: they come from 4 STANDALONE media nodes (`section>media`) which go through `buildMedia` -> `readAlt(element.alt, getSeg)` — the miss-RECORDING form (tools/cnxml-inject.js:4672). Delete the renumbering entirely and those 4 alone make the module incomplete -> SKIPPED -> line 103 still red. Two positive controls in the same run prove the instrument separates the causes: m68667's 6 misses are `entry:auto-N` ONLY (no alts), and m68670 has 5 missing `alt:` ids that record NO miss (the `ctx.peekSeg` branch, cnxml-inject.js:2821) and is written COMPLETE. So 'an alt is missing' is not automatically a miss; the discriminator is the standalone-media path, which I verified from m68690's own structure tree (4 of its 10 alt-bearing nodes are `section>media`; the other 6 are figure/example/exercise-nested).

Therefore the failing assertion is a fixture whose chosen 'later healthy module' stopped being healthy because more was extracted — the MECHANICAL shape. The A2-b mechanism is intact, which I re-proved by execution rather than accepting: the loop emits verdict lines for every module after the throw, m68670 (which sorts after m68664) is still written, exit is 1, and the '1/7 module(s) FAILED' summary and residue manifest are both produced.

WHY THE LABEL MATTERS. Filed as REGRESSION with 'no edit', this test stays red as a reminder about a defect it does not measure. That is CLAUDE.md's 'if you notice document B is wrong, fix B — never log it as a to-do in document A', and it has a second cost the finding did not price: a file left deliberately red stops being read, so the A2-b isolation contract goes unchecked from the moment the red is unrelated to A2-b. That is QUIET arriving through the back door. The auto-N misalignment is real and must be filed — in the active register as its own §C82 item, which is the ONE owner of open work.

SECOND CORRECTION — THE PROPOSED EDIT. Do not adopt the conditional swap OUT('m68690') -> OUT('m68670'). m68670's COMPLETE status rests entirely on 5 missing alts riding the peekSeg silent path, i.e. on the very readAlt/peekSeg asymmetry the finding itself flags as a defect. Unify that class in the miss-recording direction and m68670 goes incomplete and this test goes red again; unify it the other way and the finding's own warning (modules move refused -> silently written) applies. Assert the PROPERTY instead of naming a module's output file:
  OLD: expect(existsSync(OUT('m68690'))).toBe(true); // a later healthy module still injected
  NEW: expect(`${r.stdout}${r.stderr}`).toMatch(/^m68690: /m); // the loop reached a module AFTER the throw
This keeps the exact discriminating power of the original (see evidence: it is again the ONLY assertion that fails under the `break` mutant) and is immune to corpus drift, so it needs no re-baselining the next time a module gains a segment.

WHAT I CONFIRM, NOT DISPUTE (with a stronger instrument): the auto-N renumbering is real and reproduced by VALUE, and the 'silent write set = 0' claim survives a MORE CONSERVATIVE predicate than the finding used. I also add provenance evidence the finding did not have and which is stronger than its ordinal argument: the committed IS id-set is IDENTICAL to the pre-run (34f870ac^) EN id-set for 170 of 170 chemistry modules, which is what licenses old-EN-vs-new-EN as the correct diff and proves the MT was keyed to exactly the superseded extraction.

THREE SMALLER CORRECTIONS. (1) Numbers: over the same 170 modules, counting auto-N SEGMENT IDS whose EN text changed against the pre-run vintage, I get 2,514 over 59 modules — of which 4 modules (m68861, m68864, m68871, m68809; 11 ids) are marker-DIALECT drift at a STABLE id (`{{fn}}X{{/fn}}` -> `[[fn:X|foot-NNNNN]]`), i.e. the same element, not a renumbering. Netting those out gives 55 modules, the finding's number by a different route. Within noise; no conclusion moves. (2) The canary is load-bearing on NON-alt misses, not on 'missing>0'. m68809 is the worked example: its only missing ids are 3 `alt:` ids, so a naive 'missing>0 => refused' would count it loud when it may well be written. If `buildMedia`'s readAlt(…, getSeg) is 'fixed' to stop recording misses, the completeness gate weakens AS A CANARY and modules can move refused -> silently written. That sharpens the finding's subordinate item rather than contradicting it. (3) 'the ONLY red signal in the suite that points at 2,532 corrupted lookups' is a claim about 16 files made from one file and is not supportable from this file's evidence — m68667 (6 auto-N orphans, zero alt misses) is a purer carrier of the same signal and may well surface in another file's tests.

OUT OF SCOPE, for the register: duplicate segment ids exist in the committed segment files (m68690 EN: 251 SEG markers, 246 unique; IS: 241/236), and inject prints 'Note: 5 duplicate segment(s) skipped (first-match-wins)'. Id-keyed lookup being first-match-wins is a second route to a wrong value.
